validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: this row's OWN gem.wiki citation trail is exactly the pattern the task brief calls an existence flag -- all three cited URLs (vtg.com.ua 'Projects of gas transport facilities' general listing, tsoua.com 'Key Facts' company overview, a LinkedIn company page) are generic/aggregate pages about the Ukrainian gas-transmission operator in general and do NOT name 'Bohorodchany-Dolyna' specifically; two of the three (vtg.com.ua, tsoua.com/en/about-us/key-facts/) are also now dead/blocked live (404 and 403 respectively). So the sheet had zero pipeline-specific sourcing. However, independent open-web search recovered genuine, pipeline-specific, non-GEM evidence: a May 2014 State Emergency Service (DSNS) incident report -- an explosion occurred ~30m from this pipeline during repair work on the adjacent Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod trunk (km 4266, Rozhniativ district, Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast) -- was carried by two separately-published Ukrainian outlets (kp.ua and korrespondent.net), both explicitly naming 'газопровід Богородчани-Долина' / 'Bohorodchany-Dolyna gas pipeline' and describing it as a high-pressure trunk pipeline of 1400 mm diameter operating at 50-54 atm, maintained at the time by the 'Bohorodchanske LVUMG' (Bohorodchany Linear Production Department of Trunk Gas Pipelines, Prykarpattransgaz). This independently confirms EXISTENCE, matches Diameter=1400mm exactly, and geographically ties the route to Bohorodchany (Rozhniativ district sits between Bohorodchany and Dolyna in Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast) -- consistent with GEM's Start/EndLocation. CAVEAT: both news articles report near-identical facts/wording and plainly trace to one underlying DSNS press statement, so this counts as ONE independent origin, not two -- tier medium, not high. A THIRD lead was found but could NOT be verified/cited: a search-engine cached snippet of utg.ua's (Ukrtransgaz's) own 'gas quality determination route' technical document #458 explicitly titles it 'Газопровід Богородчани-Долина' and references 'Долинське ЛВУМГ' (Dolyna Linear Production Department) -- this would be a genuinely independent second origin from the current operator's own technical documentation, but the PDF itself returns HTTP 404 (utg.ua) / 403 (tsoua.com's mirror of the same document) live, and Wayback Machine lookups were rate-limited (429) throughout this pass -- flagging for a follow-up attempt rather than fabricating a citation. LENGTH: 42.00 km could not be independently corroborated by any source found; not contradicted either -- left UNRESOLVED (see fills). CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as a gas transmission trunk, not a gathering/feeder line -- both news sources describe it as a 'магістральний газопровід високого тиску' (high-pressure trunk gas pipeline) at 50-54 atm, consistent with transmission. DUPLICATE CHECK against the roster's 'Dolyna hub' cluster (P1462 Bilche-Wolitz-Dolyna 68km/1400mm; P3484/P5938 Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna I/II 292km/1220mm; P0779 Torzhok-Smolensk-Mazyr-Dolyna 1300km/1420mm) -- REFUTED as a duplicate of any of these. Bilche-Wolitz is a distinct gas field/locality from Bohorodchany (different start point, same diameter but different length -- a separate spur, not the same segment); the Ivatsevichy-Kobryn-Dolyna and Torzhok-...-Dolyna lines are much longer cross-border trunks (Belarus/Russia origin) terminating at the same hub with different diameters. Dolyna is independently confirmed (via a general Ukrainian GTS-route article, artedu.uz.ua) to host significant underground gas storage and compressor capacity in the Ivano-Frankivsk/Carpathian corridor, which is consistent with multiple distinct local spurs and long-haul trunks converging on one hub rather than any of them being the same physical pipe as P1463. fills.researcher_notes: This row's original wiki citation for ownership (tsoua.com/en/about-us/key-facts/) is now dead (403 live). Per country-standing guidance, Ukraine's entire gas transmission system has been operated/owned by the unbundled state entity 'Gas TSO of Ukraine' (GTSOU, under holding company MGU) since 1 Jan 2020, replacing Naftogaz's Ukrtransgaz -- established once at the country level, applied here. Confirmed via CEENERGYNEWS (Apr 2023 trade-press article naming GTSOU's CEO Dmytro Lyppa discussing the company's modernisation of 'Ukraine's gas transmission system' with the Deputy Minister of Energy) and GTSOU's own LinkedIn company page (confirms the entity's current existence as 'certified operator of the gas transmission system of Ukraine'). Neither source is pipeline-specific (no source names P1463 by name in connection with ownership), so this is a country-level attribution, not a segment-specific one -- tier medium. No Gazprom-ownership concern here: this row lies wholly inside Ukraine, consistent with the country rule that Gazprom holds no Ukrainian-territory section.
